notes: robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (only /checkout/ and /confirmation/ blocked); direct HTTP fetch used throughout, no browser needed. Discovery: sitemap.xml -> main_sitemap.xml (full 136KB category+facet URL list covering the entire /browse/ tree) grepped case-insensitively for christmas/xmas/halloween/easter/valentine/diwali/festive/holiday/new-year/thanksgiving/seasonal/wreath/advent/mother/father/bonfire/guy-fawkes/eid/ramadan - only Christmas slugs exist anywhere on the site; zero matches for every other holiday in the discovery vocabulary (also checked sd_sitemap.xml, same result). Habitat's own taxonomy has two separate, unconnected Christmas branches (no single root 'Christmas' node uniting them): (1) /browse/christmas-decorations/ and (2) /browse/home-furnishings/christmas-homewares/. Each PLP's exact qty taken from the page's own rendered header (data-test=result-count), which is the site's live/current count as of 2026-09-03 (off-season for Christmas, so some sub-categories show very few live products right now - Christmas baubles and Christmas tree decorations each show only 1 rendered product despite the page's internal catalog-metadata field 'productsInCategory' listing higher stale figures (12 and 44 respectively) that do not match the actual rendered product grid; the rendered header was trusted per the qty priority order). Christmas decorations (parent, own rendered count 146) does not equal its 8 children's sum (156, natural overlap) but is still recorded as a grouping row per the parent/subset convention used elsewhere in this project (near-total union of children, not a distinct independent listing). Christmas homewares (parent, 46) exactly equals the sum of its 4 children (16+9+11+10=46), confirming it is a pure aggregate and likewise recorded as a grouping row. Confirmed no duplicate/overlapping PLP URLs between the two branches. Site-internal search (/search/) returned 404 for every query tried via direct HTTP (client-side-only search, not reachable without a browser); absence of other holidays is instead established via the exhaustive full-site sitemap scan described above, which is a stronger check than search discrimination.
